[2] Longing's triumph and paradox: Śiva-din winners, bolted city unknocked, face-lotus hunger, serfdom fitness, unheard wail, omens, Śiva-night, sapless overlordship, tough self-bond, worshiper-shaped God (vv14-25).

paragraphs.text: It starts low and honest. Mind, fickle as you are, you still get praised — because you court the refuge of refuges, the worlds teacher, Ambika’s husband. I climbed past the stairs of all the lesser gods and reached Shiva’s feet — and I still have not quit the low ground. Strange, but true. So the only prayer is: show me Your road, and shutter all world-doings tight, while I am Your ever-risen servant.

Then praise and petition, rapid-fire. Four names cried out: Shiva, Shiva, Shambhu, Shankara. Dissolved in His foot-lotus seat, making even the world taste good — laughing at Viriñchi, office-smeared and unmastered. Nothing shows apart from His light-body, so He is always already won, though far by nature. His foot-sap tastes stale to some, fresh-poured to others — shining, whole-bodied, void of two. My mind glints like lightning at dawn; if it would only hold steadier, worship would be complete. Thing or unthing — is anything beyond this? As You are, be bare to me. Set walking on His own road, why do I walk so ordinarily, knowing nothing worthy of His feet? Some god of His blooms in their hearts; His story-cloud thunders and its birds sing long. Love grows fat on play in Him, till parting-grounds fruit a union-feast. His word, watered by strange sap, slips even into slant hearts, its errand ever fresh.

Then longing wins out, paradox and all. They win on whose faces the Shiva-din circles. The fierce world as good as done, mind-stain thinned to nothing — yet not one atom of knocking at His city door. Hungry for one gaze into His ever-blooming face-lotus heart: flash facing me, just a little. Why does this slave go the wrong road, forsaking her — thought of His undifference, the only glory? Never unfit for His serfdom, unless sipping undifference-wine forever. Folk truly do not see His body, dirtied by two-sight — yet shelter-tender, do You not hear my wail? Remember any sense-joy I ever asked for? No — give only body-beholding nectar, my one wish. Give it. Hundreds of fair omens rose when I stepped on His road — what more could I hunt? What a Shiva-night reigns where sun goes down with moon. Three worlds’ overlordship I count sapless without His foot-touch nectar. Tough, this self-bond, tied by You alone — scorning You first, it slackens not one jot. And God-king, worshipped by the great, still stands worshiper-shaped alone, flashing in seers’ bodies, ever.

ESSENCE: [0] Approaching touches: foot-brush joined, dust-dyed hair, dumb dwelling, shouted dance, half-shut gaping, mountain-mind, Her town, opening heart-lotus (vv1-8). [1] Tasting deepens: wax mind, bursting pot, oozing cool, lake-diving, offered passions, sated glance, straw worship, unparted feasting, secondless fullness (vv9-17). [2] Vows and vastness: foot-place won, perfume hardened, clash taught, frenzy willed, vanguard run, unre-said sap, vast roamed, dust-kept thought, sole-touchers shown (vv18-26).

paragraphs.text: Approaching happens in touches. Wedded in joy by the mere brush of His lotus-feet: take me by the scruff into Your house. Hair dyed red with His foot-lotus dust: when do I break into boundless frenzied dance? This much I beg and nothing else: dumb, dwelling inside You I may be — never otherwise, O Wise One. Ah nectar-hoard, ah sweet Three-eyed, ah tasty Deformed-eyed: so may I dance, yelling. Eyes half-shut with His foot-lotus touch: may I gape wide, reeling with His love-wine’s drunkenness. Mind-mountain on earth, may I dwell anywhere where that practice runs unbroken, deep-sapped, made of His babble. Where He stands with the Lady, many-shaped, from palace to gate-tower: in that town may I dwell. May His sun-rays sport, Lord, till this heart-lotus of mine opens — for His worship.

Then tasting deepens. Be gracious: may my mind, ever fallen at His feet, tasting this and that, melt as wax, run. From joy though it blow pot-lids, or from sorrow — from outward feeling, inward feeling — show plain to me, Master. Without within: may that ever-oozing be mine, His foot-lotus-touch nectar, cool past cool. Dived deep in His touch-nectar lake: O what a joy past joys, leaping all enjoyment — be mine, ever. Take the laid offering, passions and the rest, take, nectarize, and feast — with lover-folk together. Ever sated on whole-world food, easy-seated: take among servants one grace-glance-instant, Master. Half-eyed chewing inner love-wonder — bow to me, to Shiva — worshiping, may I be even straws. Though His state be won, seeing the world my self-blaze, by love-sap feastings may I stay unparted. Since naught else is to be longed for: His, secondless — fullness is but fit.

Then vows and vastness. Where laughter and dancing happen, where hates-and-loves are eaten and love-nectar drunk: may I win that foot-place. That unheard perfume, His-thought-blossoms’ scent, harden in my mind till ill-habit’s stink is eaten. Where, pray, love among passions — and where love among His foot-lotuses? Teach my clash-fond heart its good, Deathless One. Roaming yoga-states even, turned from sense-things even: His-thought-wine’s frenzy liquifying my heart, only that may I be. Speech, mind-thoughts, sense-wrought body-moves: everywhere, ever, may love-sap run vanguard before me. Shiva Shiva Shiva muttered without end: tasting may I be some unrepeatable sap. Vast flashing endless knowing-self, dull roads all drunk dry: honored, may I roam ramparts uncounted, knowing-made. Standing in self-body, clear-shining, everlasting: naught else avails. Firm be this thought — yet His foot-lotus dust, O Pure. Something, Lord, sometime flashes in mind: touchers of His foot-sole, where this whole melts — in nectar’s lake show me this world, ever.

Weary — thereby, by no effort, may I win You everywhere.

paragraphs.text: Grace nears from both sides at once: a grace-drop, Lord-abiding, and devotion as if nearing to meet me — the two, each in other. When will they take root in such a body? Born of chewing Your mastery whole, may some contentment-sap rise within. Here, always, be highest for me: knowledge, yoga, glories far off. Worldlike be my thirst among sense-things, swollen full, utter, Lord. Only as Your body may I behold them — I, thought-unbuilt.

Then the senses get gathered. In body-grounds, in mind, Lord, where breath’s run has met difference, and on those knowing-paths: thereby, by Your own self, be plain to me. May these thrilled sense-plays of mine fall each to its own seat — never, Lord, not an instant, not a jot, the outrage: wounding Your undifference-sap. Light, soft, white, clear, cool: by Your possession-force picturing a body, may I stride past those dealings of the all-things’ road.

Then blooming and union. Bloom, my body, Thou-natured; come, worlds, to my limbhood. Pass, all this two-sport — though on memory’s road it come — to untellability. Rise, O glance at such a face of Thine: highest-nectar deluge, befall me, till filled the dread gorge of Your unshown oneness. If ever, dusted thinnest with Your meeting-nectar-drops, I turn not from all world-joys — or fallen from both — what then? I, choice hamsa, ever wading Your foot-lotus-lake: above, from root-depth, from within, bend up, love’s lotus-stalk, O Unborn. Come, All, all things: under thought’s reach, under sight’s footing for me; sight-thought-shine-nectar-piths, shimmer supreme. High-Lord, in strait on strait, when names themselves bow down: may I be not merely fear-gone but, Your limbs lending, joy-mad past measure. Woven in Your self, the world — by You alone shown outside. What hard resolve holds: now may it shine plain.

Then dwelling deepens. In Your foot-lotus’s belly dissolved, melted of other-longing: honey-overmuch, sated, may I roam at will. Whose resolve to worship You rose from sham even: for him needs must dawn Your fit nearness. Lord: mind past others-hoping, one-sapped utterly — the easy, all-outlying Lord to sating may I drink. Things be as things by Your being, for me. So be naught elsewise: naught but Thine. What is naught at all, be naught at all; something at all, be something indeed for me. May I be: but brimming-love-wine-sap-mad. Who, dragging the outside into heart’s inside itself, worships Thee, Ruler: with love-nectar-sap-floods him I bow. Between right and unright selves, between doings, between knowings: so between joy-and-pain selves, lovers taste some. Ah! Gleaners, grain-pickers, foes’ shadow-limbed even, Ruler: by Thy-love’s great heat the king of kings even they lord. In nectar-wet Thy-love though wallowing, yet climb-hungering: with mind alone, All, some worship Thee, standing round about.

Kept and questioned next. To be guarded, to be grown, to be honored: this, Ruler, passing’s ill-faring-smasher, Thy love’s great hoard. Lord, though Thy lover-folk love Thee: yet envy dropped toward Her, gladdened ever be the Mistress. Thy state first, to be: when Thy love’s birth-time comes, won the milk-great jar; slain, in curds, greed. What, is this not attainment past compare? What chief joy streams it not? Love, ever-waxing: this, the Kind One’s, ever-new. In Thy stained mind sunk, Thy-love’s gem-creeper: hard! spreads not even its own, those unmanned own-hoard-blossomings. Love in the Lord, in three-worlds’ Master: is it not highest attainment? Yet for want of wonder-powers, is it not full? This, my worry.

Then pervasion and road. Without, within too: keen-blooming Three-eyed’s-bouquet-scents, fair, scent even cross-scented yogins, near-dwelling, all. Light is there, by no tale, none; the world even, all past-sleep. Where, Lord, at Shiva-night’s post, ever lover-folk worship Thee. Goodness, in true mood, in kindly Lord, widen in worship. On the crown sport Kind-Maker’s-foot-dust-risen-heaps. To sever passion-and-the-rest mind-scents even, gloom gape, Kind One, be mine: or in Thy-self-loss, the three-strand-throng. Passing’s road far-far; limb-stalk burnt with keen-and-sundry ills; joys nowise tasted; what joy was, never long was ours. Thus vain am I grown: moon-bearer’s-foot-pressed-fair-crowned, and Thy lover. So make me now: high-fortuned, long-long.

For lovers naught to be felt: in Thee within, or without — where Thou, knowing-natured, doubtfree standest, Thyself. Lovers, at blame-mimicked even, thrill: by Thy nectar-drops, as if, inward-pierced by keen thrill-needles. Pain-feeling even, for lovers, ripens to feasting: whose knowing, all of it, nectar-wet, is Thy-moonshine-made. Where-go held, of lovers, without-within: guileless, Thy-frame-touch-sap-taste-joy same. Lord, in Thy love’s worship, the abject share that leans on two wiped out, some savor a frame clear, nectar-made. Astray, ford-seers, split: for split is but straying’s. Foeless, thing one: for lovers Thou shinest. Mind stainless-ripe past honor, scorn, love and the rest: whose is he, the lover? World-like-mannered how could he be? Love-hate-gloom even, whose love-shine conquered: before those great ones, which are the knowing-rich? Whose rite-and-means is love-nectar-bath-and-drink: his, in begun-middle-end states, high ease-seat. Praised be, sought be, worshiped be: whereby Thou alone, of Thy lovers, praised be world-faring, Thee-made.

Then freedom, then seal. Freedom’s name is but ripe love in Thee, Lord. Thereon, first-stage-mounted, freed-like are we. Pain’s coming even, great be mine, love-brimmed-souled. From-Thee-turned, All, never: joy’s train even. Thou by love art gladdened; love, gladdened in Thee: and, Lord, since that mutual-ground is fit, as Thou alone knowest it. Shaped or shapeless, in or out even: to lover-selves, Ruler, ever art Thou nectar-made. In this world itself, within, toward Thy lover: joy-showing-fruited, another world-stand stands. In the hidden, love; in the high, love; in the world’s Great Lord, love: in Thee, Kind One, in Shiva — love, forsooth, some! Ah! Love, love: high love, fierce love indeed! From knower to known, on whose feeling-road by Thee no parting is: they win, Thy partakers. Outside passing’s hall, by some art Thou clasped: Master. Dealings success-giving, all, whose vanguard is Your worship. Lovers, Thee-made, themselves ripe attainments. Ever, in all states, at once, all-shaped: they worship restless, and they are my gods. Touch-Thee-feast, ripe by scorning thought-strain: worship’s rule, so famed, be mine ever. Lovers’ evenness-pith-equinox-tide, ever: by Thy-state-sap-nectar-sap, their ever-worship. Whose start-and-end are not, nor time-rank, Ruler: worship-selved is that deed; its doers, Thy partakers, merely. BrahmA-and-first ones even, rulers, fortune-sharers: in whose dream even, swoon even, stands Thy worship-feast. Mutterers, offerers, bathers, thinkers — and not barely: lovers’ Thee-worship, ah, as-far, when, then. Tasting Your worship-nectar-joy-wedding, glad, ever: mid Indra-and-first, ay, BrahmA-chiefs — is who their match? At Thy worship-high-feast, sole-born of world-churn: what won is won, some; lovers alone ken it.

Then the feast gets entered. In Thy knowing-made seat standing, by six-and-thirty-principle-deeds: by body-speech-mind-stirs and the rest, worship I Thee ever, All. Glad in Thy-worship-woven-clinging-wedding, of me: fare, time, all, ay, endless. This I pray. Greed for Thy-worship-nectar-sap-feasting: All! Wax day on day, and ever fruit, for me. In Thine ocean, brimmed with world-play-nectar-one-sap: Thee, high-souled, worshiping may I sit, ever. Ever plain by all-hankering-knot-severing: may mind be laid before Thee by lovers, sweet, in Thy worship-rule. Standing upon these sense-fields, sense-plays of lovers send: for Thy-worship-sake, nectar-wine. Lovers, love-surge-great-heat-helpless-souled: what other freedom-cause, but drowning in Thy-worship-nectar? Ever, Thy-foot-honoring-nectar-drink-high-feast: my Thy-grace-one-winning cause, may it avail. May I feel, Ruler, deed by deed, wink by wink: Thy-worship-nectar-drink-frenzy-taste-high-glee. Seen-fruited indeed is lovers’ Thy-worship-high-venture: at once, unthinkable joy they taste. While unwon, Thy-worship-high-feast: while, untasted I deem a speck even of joy’s hoard. Lovers’, without sense-hunt-shine-strain even: strain-free-ripe, Thy seat-standing in worship is born.

Then the feast deepens. Naught to win is there for lovers, nor aught scarce to them. Merely roam they: Thy-worship-wine-frenzy-mad. Ah! love-heavy-open-hearted: love, Ruler! Toward Thee: praised, the worship-rule, somehow — by begging unstained. What beauty is not, what glee not, what thrive not, or else: what freedom not, since this Great God is worshiped? Inward-sporting-clear-fed, Thy love-fed: for Thy-worship’s use be mine this frame. Thy-foot-worship-wedding-bound ever, All: may I be, worlds’ Ruler, alone, free-stirring. Somehow wins, Master: Thy worship-high-feast, where of six-and-thirty principles even churn sports amply. Bow to them, All: whose, by love-nectar-water, hallowed themselves turn Thy worship-gear even. At worship’s start, All: thought on, mantra-laid Thy selfness, in self alone, high, lovers shine with glee — nowhither. By kingdom-winning-and-the-rest-blooming ones at Thy worship-high-feast: with nectar-wine the all-earth is shared out. Worship-nectar-drink-made, whose feasting wink by wink: are they gods? Are they freed? Or whatever folk indeed?

Then the feast gets sealed. By world-turned-worship-gear-guise, weight. Ah! some of lovers and some indeed lightness. From worship-made-glance-toss-churn alone, nectar-upcoming: for lovers; as milk-sea-churn for sky-dwellers. Worship some deem a wish-cow. Nectar-stream-over-sapped, suck the inward-faced others. Lovers’ glance-toss even — this, passing-approved — fetching some within, fattens the worship-high-feast. By love-churn’s force, Ruler, worship in Thee, self-become. Strange: for abjectness’ high fruit. Courtesy-tread is worship, for some, to win Thy feet. For lovers, Thine-one-self-bliss-spread is it. By unbound-mad-love’s unbarred — worship of unjoined-shape even — spread out, it wins a stand in Thee, some. Mind stilled by tasting sweet-love-sap: fallen, beauteous. Kind One: Thou alone, lovely, art worship’s bowl, they say. Brimmed, pure, loving, steady: in Thy worship-rule, Ruler, means be mine. Tasting Your worship-nectar-joy-wedding, glad, ever: mid Indra-and-first, ay, BrahmA-chiefs — is who their match? But mind, risen this even, kens not self-shape here. Ah! then — ah! — I am slain. Thy feet honored with full wealth, won by dwelling in Thee-made self: who needs neither food nor cloak ever — to him bowed am I. Ever in Thy-frame-dwelling hale, yet inside supremely burns this world. By Thy will, so do for me that here, Thy-worship-joy-made, I be.

Dwelling images, one after another. By own sap risen: Thy-lotus-feet-pair-worship-nectar-drink-glued-mind — in all-aims’-gatherings may I be: touch-joy alone for world-faring. In the whole field of dealings, plainly, while You throb inside, Lord: coming and going ever, may my things shine always. Ever in Thine own city — or cityless, roaming with Thee: not a wink’s crumb even be mine of defeat, forsooth, where Thee-made. In Thy-limb-oozed well-cool-nectar-floods brimmed, all round even: in Thy-worship-wealth here, Thy lovers in passing’s lake within roam. In great-chant-tree-shade-cool, in Thy high woods, in mine own self ever, Ruler: may I dwell, Thy honorer. To each thing of all breathers Thou dawnest, dawn-made, as. Dwelling in high-nectar-sea’s middle, in Thy-honor-rule alone sunk-mind: all folk-faring may I ply, savoring, everything indeed, aught even.

Then paradox, then entry. Thine here, be thing, be truth: to bare it, who here is vessel fit? This alone: name-shape-stir-and-the-rest-unequalled of Thine — takes. Taker art Thou, since. Wake-or-other-state, or high even: whatever even, a jot of standing — for love-bowl-folk, all is Thou-lorded-mind’s high feast. Mind: eye-ring courses, everywhere loosened yet still — Thee winning, hard-long-knowing, Ruler: by love-hoard’s heat, how? Nor sundered was unmade aught, yet unjoy was never built. Thought-stain washed bright by splashed denial-blade-nectar-flood: doubt-foe unconquered crushed — Thy beholding be unbroken. Plain, enter me: then may I enter, ever, Ruler — Thine am I, since. With rush Thy frame itself: outright, high-neared, may I honor. In Thee no praise-might is any one’s — or is indeed, since passing fair art Thou. Ever again my begging is this: that restless I behold the Ruler.

paragraphs.text: Prayer grounds first: past-grounds, one-hoard selves, knowing-frames, pain-thieved farings. Beyond prayer-grounds, strange-fruit-giver: victorious, unprecedented-storied, Shiva the wish-tree.

Then face and melting. When will foot-thought-jewel-creeper-fruition, amazing the perfected, befall me, from You? When, Lord, shall I fully see Your pure face-orb, from which streams unprecedented-nectar-flood, drowning the world whole? Your form, risen at mere meditation — when, Lord, will it ever fill my far gaps with unprecedented-nectar floods? By touch of Your peerless rasa, unroaming abandoned: not now is my mind, Lord. When will it be? Let it be soon. Not dry-bitter things only: nay, all, always — to You offered, gained: even opposites rush me. Lord, may Your pure rays come face to face, as long as body-mind-heat-dark is wiped out. God, be gracious till my path-blockers, truth-stealing, sense-thieves are tamed. With Your devotion-nectar-essence fill my mind fast, Lord: till these are carried off, drowned — all sapless hankerings.

Then freedom and Master. In liberation-state, where is devotion to You — how could it even shine for the mortal-natured? Nay. So me, Unborn, on a fitting attainment-ground raise. Greedy for a siddhi-drop’s gain, with smugness settle me not: starved, before Your devotion-face, is freedom; sprouting wonder-wings. May the Lord be pleased with me, His slave — this much alone I beg. In mind brimmed with Your frame-mindfulness-nectar-sap: Your lotus-feet-pair in mine, blooming be ever — honey-oozing, beyond the world. Mine is the Master, yonder: father, then Three-eyed, then mother BhavAnI. No second here, whoever is mine: thus most-fulfilled may I roam.

I praise, self-forgetting, white-robed in bite-torn cloth, dancing to the tune of the skull-garland: feast-ready. Bow to those whose god is Hara, whose stirs are Hara-fit, Hara-alone-bent breaths ever: fortune’s houses. Your play, behind lordship — and this too, as wished-fulfilled in gifts, by self I reach the supreme means. In Your world-venerated abode, in this play: how great would my bliss-birth be?

The paradox middle. How could He not be fortunate — who is Gauri’s lover, Hara? And how could Hara not be Gauri’s supreme beloved? Whose meditation-nectar is undying, self-rooted, ever-fresh: consciousness-creepers, like some being-tree. At devotion-itch’s showing, Lord’s pillar-firmness arises: by it the world, great festival, is won. Ever to creation-sport, ever seated in staying-pleasure, ever world-eating-sated: to the Master, bow. Nowhere gone, nothing left: who just this, see Your abode as to-be here — fortunate: to them bow, bow. For the devotion-fortuned, what else is begged; for the devotion-poor, what else is begged? Where pains turn pleasures, poison turns nectar, saṃsāra turns liberation: that path is He, Kind-Maker. At root, middle, end: no suffering for Your people — yet we sink, Lord: tell why?

The closing seal. Light is worth begging even by beginners in knowledge-yoga: You, Lord of devotees, are like the light of the free. Devotees have no prayers, no remembrance of You the self — yet this Shiva of theirs, something, on the lip. Who lights all appearances, wrapped in vimarsha: I am this — so I praise Your action-power, Lord. All beings, from BrahmA to Vishnu, being devoured: so I bow, God, to the world as Your-formed. All beyond me is false, by relation to destruction: thus engaged, Lord, by Your destruction-play alone. Meditated, Your form stands present for devotion-rich: unconquered by unthinkable-wonder-makers. By Your devotion-wine-taste nerves’ thrill, night-heroes dance, roused by vetAlas. The praise begun with this limb of mine: by it may all this time be firmly unending.
